title: Replicable Fine-Spatio-Temporal Climate Data for Long-Term Ecology in the Western Mediterranean
problem: Obtaining fine spatio-temporal climate data for past periods is challenging, as existing datasets often suffer from either coarse spatial resolution, limiting their use in regional studies, or sparse temporal coverage, which prevents the analysis of continuous long-term ecological patterns.
method: We propose a statistical downscaling toolkit using a perfect prognosis approach with Generalized Linear Models to generate fine-resolution, long-term climate reconstructions by creating a transfer function between coarse-resolution climate simulations and fine-resolution historical data.
task: The task is to downscale coarse-resolution climate datasets for the Western Mediterranean from 22 ka BP to 2100 using a new R-based toolkit, creating a fine-resolution climate dataset for long-term ecological studies.
innovation: This paper presents a replicable R-based toolkit and a high-resolution (11x11 km, monthly) downscaled climate dataset for the Western Mediterranean, providing continuous data from 22,000 years BP to 2100 to support long-term ecological and paleoclimatic research.

Similarly, the TraCE-21ka project used a coupled atmosphere-ocean GCM (Community Climate System Model version 3) to estimate global monthly climate data since the LGM, providing a foundation for other projects aiming to increase spatial resolution (e.g., PaleoView, CHELSA-TraCE21k) or the number of variables available (e.g., CHELSA-TraCE21k).

It was subsequently used to downscale monthly climate reconstructions from the LGM (22 ka BP; 1000 years before the end of the LGM) to future projections (up to 2100 cal years), using data from the TraCE-21ka project, the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 5 (CMIP5), and the UERRA reanalysis project. This process yielded a high-resolution dataset for the Western Mediterranean region, both spatially and temporally (DS-TraCE-21ka).
